newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower after profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower after profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan shares prices closed lower on Saturday after late profit-taking from previous day's gains, brokers said.
The weighted index slide 51.25 points or 0.66 percent to 7,739.94. Turnover was an hectic T$158.79 billion.
"Investors busily sold their shares to bag profits following their previous day's gains, thus pulling down the index," said Allen Huang, a manager of National Securities.
The market, backed by plastic and electronic shares, opened sharply up in early trade, undisturbed by the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping on Wednesday, brokers said.
But heavy profit-taking pulled the foreign fund-favored electronic sector down sharply by 4.55 percent in the last trading hour, with computer giant Acer losing T$3.50 at T$59.50, brokers said.
Brokers, however, said the Taiwan bourse was expected to maintain its upward trend next week.
"The apparent government behind-the-scene support of the local bourse is seen to beef up the market," said Oliver Rang of National Securities.
The index was expected to range between 7,600 and 7,800 points next week, he said.
The death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had little impact on the market as most players focused on domestic fundamentals, brokers said.
"The uptrend has not changed yet because market liquidity is still quite sufficient at this moment," said Albert Lin, research manager of Golden Securities.
However, brokers agreed that investors would carefully watch any fresh developments in China for their next move.
Trading interest was likely to focus on asset-backed shares and blue chips, they said.
